x: Charlie Melchior and George Powell have again been the backbone of the Club with their Javelin performances allied to their participation in the Shot Putt and Discus.
Eddie Pack was Southern and Inter-Counties 440 yards Champion, and runner-up in the A.A.A. title. Charlie Melchior was second in the Southern and third in the A.A.A.

This loss meant that the brunt of the Shot event fell upon Charlie Melchior. He has gained us useful points in all matches and did a personal best of 34 ft. 8 ins. in the match against the Police at Imber Court.
Javelin.—1 C.
McKenzie was second for us in the High Jump, thus showing his versatility, Charlie Melchior won the Javelin, and Bill Sutton had a couple of second places in the Weight and Discus.
Weight.—1 C.

Our Javelin throwers, Charlie Melchior, Alan Dunn and veteran George Powell have not shown performances up to their best, but Charlie again won the Hertfordshire County Championship and the Club Championship with a throw of 154 feet 3 inches.
George Lucas lost a close race by inches in the Kent County 3 miles race in record time, and Charlie Melchior won the Javelin Throw in the Hertfordshire event.
C.

Charlie Melchior and George Powell. However, it is to Alan Dunn, Geoff Jarvis, Arthur Allen and Terry Bateman we look for improved performances and from at least one, distances approaching, even if not beating those achieved by the old stalwarts in previous years.

In the Javelin we shall no doubt see our old stalwart George Powell performing again and also Charlie Melchior. If Alan Dunn is now fully recovered from his arm injury he should be our first string backed up by Bateman, Higgins and Bergvalds.
Bergvalds, our Latvian member, scored points for us in the Weight Put and Discus Throw, but we missed the help of Charlie Melchior in the Javelin Throw.
Bergvalds retained his Weight and Discus titles and Charlie Melchior once again won the Javelin Throw.

Charlie Melchior again won the championship, which shows the paucity of good performers. Terry Bateman will, we hope, show considerable improvement, and with Doug Whitehead, now back in “civvy street” aftr getting a R.A.F.
Sutton, C.
Harris won the Discus Throw with C. Melchior second and Bill Sutton third, but the throwing was not up to standard and no one beat a 100 feet.
Javelin.—C.
